actual_scope: Audit PR2162 section 3 split min-max and its universal perfect-split corollary using one precisely cited linking-system theorem and independent exact finite certificates.
scope_change_reason: The explicit donor assigned adversarial mathematical audit, rather than the catalogue default. This is a side result on structural decoder proof machinery, not an all-size/compiler transfer audit. Current hosting/outer-transfer claims overlapped; PR2162 itself leaves this identity quoted without a precise source, and PR2293 explicitly leaves it unchecked.
bottleneck_link: A rigorous decoder-floor implication can guide structural mechanisms that change copied-information cost. This closes one proof dependency of pending decoder research; it supplies no selected supplier, physical cost saving, or kappa improvement.
stop_rule: Prove or falsify the named min-max implication; exhaust common-B/support-mask inputs through v=2, all three arbitrary binary 2x2 blocks, and the fixed 576 larger sampled cases. No extension beyond v=5; finite coverage is not the general proof. Reserve the final quarter for source/mathematical review, package checks and submission.
evidence: PROOF.md derives the identity from Schrijver Theorem 3.6 and proves the correctly quantified universal corollary. EXPECTED.json records 70,337 input cases, 4,656 distinct block tuples, 8,701 cases satisfying the principal-cost premise, and twelve controls.

ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance for task selection, literature lookup, mathematical derivation, code, checks and packaging. Parent-only execution; no subagents or external model. Author-checked, not independently human-reviewed.
